Photos recovered from Zubair's chats with the Applicant allegedly show medicine slips and syrup bottles.

29. The Applicant, Rahul Varshney, was apprehended on 04.04.2024 following the disclosure statement of co-accused Zubair, who alleged that a portion of the recovered contraband substances had been procured from the Applicant.
30. Firstly, it has to be noted that two of the co-accused persons have already been granted Bail by this Court.
Co-accused Rekha was granted Bail vide Order dated 26.11.2024 in her Bail Application No.3901/2024.

Co- accused Ashwani Kumar @ Ashu has also been granted Bail vide Order dated 03.04.2025 in Bail Application No. 280/2025.
31.

Secondly, the evidence against him primarily consists of CDRs and the chat messages recovered from the mobile phone of co-accused Zubair, which suggest that they were in contact prior to Zubair's arrest.
The prosecution further relies on bank transaction records reflecting payments received from Saba Parbeen which were allegedly made on Zubair's instructions.

32. However, it is significant to note that there was no recovery of any contraband substance from the Applicant and the evidence to establish his involvement essentially are the CDR.
33.

The Apex Court, in State (by NCB) Bengaluru vs. Pallulabid Ahmad Arimutta, (2022) 12 SCC 633, while refusing to interfere with the order granting Bail, observed that the CDR details of some of the accused or the allegations of tampering of evidence on the part of one of the respondents, is an aspect that will be examined at the stage of trial.

The Prosecution has opposed the Bail on the ground that the Applicant was involved previously in FIR No. 40/2003 under Sections 420/468/471/485/486/120B Indian Penal Code, 1860 along with offences under the Drugs & Cosmetics Act, Trade Marks Act, and Copyright Act; and while on Bail, had committed the present offence.

However, it cannot be over looked that the said case did not pertain to any offence under the NDPS Act and there is no circumstances shown to indicate that he is likely to commit the offence of present nature, if released on bail.
38. It needs to be considered simultaneously, that even though Chargesheet/ Supplementary Charge-Sheet has already been filed, but even the Charges are yet to be framed.

39. It is opposite to refer to the decision of the Apex Court in Union of India vs. K.A. Najeeb, (2021)

40. In the decision of Manish Sisodia vs. Central Bureau of Investigation, 2023 SCC OnLine SC 139,
the Apex Court reiterated that that right of liberty guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India is a sacrosanct right which needs to be accepted even in cases where stringent provisions are incorporated through special laws.

sentences.text: It was held that prolonged incarceration before being pronounced guilty of an offence, should not be permitted to become punishment without trial.

It was further observed that fundamental right of liberty provided under Article 21 of the Constitution is superior to statutory restrictions and reiterated the principle that "bail is the rule and refusal is an exception".
41.
